title: The Gnostic and the Practical
english: Practical men will understand practical words, but Gnostics will see Gnostic things.
A practical man is one who has acquired only the passive part of the soul to be impassive.
A Gnostic, however, holds the word of salt for the impure, but of light for the pure.

The knowledge occurring to us from without attempts to point out the elements through words; but the knowledge approaching from the grace of God presents the realities to the intellect by the mind's own vision, toward which the intellect looks, and brings to them its own words; but error opposes the former, and anger and passion oppose the latter, and those following them.
All virtues make the way for the Gnostic; but above all is impassivity. For he who has grasped knowledge and is easily moved toward anger is like one piercing his own eyes with an iron probe.

Let the Gnostic be secure in his descents, lest a state of descending happen to him without his noticing, and let him constantly test all virtues equally, making them right, so that they may follow one another and be in him, because the intellect is by nature prone to be betrayed by diminution.
It is shameful for a Gnostic to judge both the one being wronged and the one doing wrong; the one being wronged because he did not endure, and the one doing wrong because he did wrong.
Knowledge, being preserved, teaches the one participating in it how he might be guarded and proceed toward greater things.

It is just for monks and for those in the world to discourse correctly concerning right conduct and to clarify in part those doctrines of natural or theological matters, without which no one will see the Lord.
Know the words and the laws of times, lives, and customs, so that you may easily say to each what is profitable.

Do not allegorize the words of false persons, nor seek anything spiritual in them, unless God has acted through economy, as in Balaam (Numbers 22:28) and Caiaphas (Matthew 27:24), so that one [speaks] concerning the birth and the other concerning the death of our Savior.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
